title: Every day he told me 먹지 마 (don't eat it)… until his last day 🥺 #learnkorean
caption:
-지 마 = don't. Put it right after a verb stem:

먹지 마 (meok-ji ma) = Don't eat it!
입지 마 (ip-ji ma) = Don't wear it!
열지 마 (yeol-ji ma) = Don't open it!
가지 마 (ga-ji ma) = Don't go…
울지 마 (ul-ji ma) = Don't cry.

Drop 지 마 and add 어 — the "don't" turns into a yes: 먹어 (meo-geo) = Eat it.

-지 마 is casual, for friends and family. To someone older or your boss, say 먹지 마세요.

pinnedComment: Who would you say 가지 마 (don't go) to? 👇
alt: A needle-felted cafe. The coral felt mascot sneaks toward a strawberry cake; the barista's palm cuts in: 먹지 마! (meok-ji ma) = Don't eat it! Behind the counter the mascot wears his huge green apron: 입지 마! (ip-ji ma) = Don't wear it! By the back door it pries open his packed suitcase: 열지 마! (yeol-ji ma) = Don't open it! (지 마 and Don't share one color.) Evening: in his coat, the barista hangs that green apron on a hook for the last time, his suitcase at his feet — his last day at the cafe. At the door the mascot says 가지 마… (ga-ji ma) = Don't go… He pats its head: 울지 마. (ul-ji ma) = Don't cry. Night, the cafe is empty: he left a note by a slice of cake. The note grows into his first scold 먹지 마! — then 지 마 and Don't fall off and it becomes 먹어. (meo-geo) = Eat it. The mascot takes a bite, crying and smiling.
